:demo-write-brief.content: Write a concise explanation of the topic below for a busy reader. Lead with the takeaway, use plain language, and stay under 120 words. Topic: [topic]

:demo-write-deep.content: Explain [topic] in depth. Start with a short overview, then cover the key ideas, an example, common mistakes, and a practical conclusion.

:demo-write-story.content: Turn this idea into a vivid short story with a clear beginning, conflict, and satisfying ending. Show emotions through actions rather than labels. Idea: [idea]

:demo-write-opinion.content: Write a balanced opinion piece on [issue]. State a clear position, acknowledge the strongest counterargument fairly, and end with a thoughtful takeaway.

:demo-write-howto.content: Create a beginner-friendly how-to guide for [task]. List prerequisites, numbered steps, a quick verification, and what to do if a step fails.

:demo-write-outline.content: Create a logical outline for an article about [topic]. Include a compelling title, main sections, key points under each, and a conclusion angle.

:demo-write-faq.content: Draft 8 useful FAQ questions and direct answers about [topic]. Prioritize questions a newcomer would actually ask.

:demo-write-speech.content: Write a three-minute speech for [audience] about [topic]. Open with a memorable hook, use one concrete example, and end with a call to action.

:demo-write-report.content: Turn these notes into a neutral report. Separate facts, assumptions, risks, and next steps. Do not invent missing details. Notes: [notes]

:demo-write-plain.content: Rewrite the text below for a general audience at an accessible reading level. Keep every important fact and remove jargon. Text: [text]

:demo-edit-proof.content: Proofread the text for spelling, grammar, and punctuation. Preserve the author's voice. Return the corrected text followed by a short list of meaningful changes. Text: [text]

:demo-edit-tight.content: Cut unnecessary words from the text while keeping its meaning and tone. Aim for roughly 30% shorter. Text: [text]

:demo-edit-clarity.content: Revise this passage for clarity. Fix ambiguous references and awkward sentence order without adding claims. Passage: [text]

:demo-edit-tone.content: Rewrite this message in a warm, professional tone. Keep the request and facts unchanged. Message: [text]

:demo-edit-formal.content: Make this text formal enough for a business document without sounding stiff. Preserve all numbers and names. Text: [text]

:demo-edit-casual.content: Make this text conversational and natural while keeping it respectful and accurate. Text: [text]

:demo-edit-inclusive.content: Review this text for unclear or exclusionary wording. Suggest more inclusive alternatives and explain only changes that matter. Text: [text]

:demo-edit-structure.content: Improve the structure of this draft. Reorder ideas for flow, add useful headings, and flag any unsupported leap. Draft: [text]

:demo-edit-headline.content: Give me 10 accurate headline options for this article: three direct, three curious, two playful, and two search-friendly. Article: [text]

:demo-edit-feedback.content: Act as a constructive editor. Identify the three strongest parts of this draft and the three highest-impact improvements, with examples. Draft: [text]

:demo-email-intro.content: Draft a friendly first-contact email to [person] about [reason]. Keep it brief, specific, and easy to reply to.

:demo-email-followup.content: Write a polite follow-up to this unanswered email. Assume one week has passed; avoid guilt or pressure. Original: [email]

:demo-email-thanks.content: Write a sincere thank-you email after [event]. Mention one concrete detail and keep it under 120 words.

:demo-email-decline.content: Decline [request] kindly and clearly. Give a brief reason only if helpful, and avoid implying a commitment I cannot make.

:demo-email-meeting.content: Draft a meeting request for [topic] with purpose, proposed duration, and two suggested times. Make the action needed obvious.

:demo-email-recap.content: Turn these meeting notes into a recap email with decisions, owners, deadlines, and unresolved questions. Notes: [notes]

:demo-email-apology.content: Write a responsible apology for [mistake]. Acknowledge the impact, explain the remedy, and avoid excuses or overpromising.

:demo-email-update.content: Write a project update email for [audience]. Use sections for progress, blockers, next steps, and requests. Facts: [facts]

:demo-email-subject.content: Suggest 12 clear subject lines for this email, from straightforward to slightly engaging. Avoid clickbait. Email: [email]

:demo-email-short.content: Reduce this email to five sentences or fewer without losing its key ask, date, or context. Email: [email]

:demo-market-audience.content: Describe three plausible audiences for [product]. For each, list the job they need done, likely objections, and where they look for information. Mark assumptions.

:demo-market-value.content: Write five distinct value propositions for [product] aimed at [audience]. Focus on outcomes, not a list of features.

:demo-market-landing.content: Draft a landing page for [product] with a clear headline, subheading, three benefits, proof placeholders, FAQ, and a low-pressure call to action.

:demo-market-cta.content: Generate 15 call-to-action labels for [offer]. Group them by direct, reassuring, and playful tone. Keep each under six words.

:demo-market-seo.content: Create a search-focused article outline for [query]. Address user intent first; include likely questions and a concise meta description. Do not claim ranking guarantees.

:demo-market-launch.content: Plan a small-budget launch for [product]. Give a two-week timeline, channels, measurable goals, and a way to learn from weak results.

:demo-market-objections.content: List common objections to [product] for [audience]. Write honest, evidence-dependent responses and note what proof is missing.

:demo-market-position.content: Compare [product] with [alternatives] using audience, strengths, trade-offs, and an honest positioning statement. Do not invent competitor facts.

:demo-market-survey.content: Write 10 unbiased customer interview questions to learn how people solve [problem] today. Avoid leading them toward our product.

:demo-market-test.content: Design a simple A/B test for [marketing idea]. Define one hypothesis, a primary metric, guardrails, and how long to wait before deciding.

:demo-social-linkedin.content: Write a thoughtful LinkedIn post about [lesson]. Use a concrete opening, short paragraphs, one practical takeaway, and no engagement bait.

:demo-social-instagram.content: Draft an Instagram caption for [photo or topic] in a warm voice. Include a useful detail, a natural question, and five relevant hashtag ideas.

:demo-social-thread.content: Turn [topic] into a six-post thread. Each post should stand on its own, build on the last, and avoid unsupported claims.

:demo-social-calendar.content: Plan one week of social posts for [brand]. Vary formats and goals; provide topic, hook, visual idea, and call to action for each day.

:demo-social-reply.content: Write a calm, helpful reply to this public comment. Acknowledge the concern, avoid arguing, and move private details to direct contact. Comment: [comment]

:demo-social-video.content: Write a 30-second vertical-video script about [topic] with an opening hook, three quick beats, on-screen text, and an ending line.

:demo-social-carousel.content: Outline a seven-slide educational carousel on [topic]. Give each slide one idea and an easy-to-read headline.

:demo-social-poll.content: Create five non-leading poll questions about [topic], each with four balanced answer options and a follow-up discussion prompt.

:demo-social-repurpose.content: Repurpose this article into a short post, a three-post thread, and a video outline. Keep the factual claims intact. Article: [text]

:demo-social-audit.content: Review these social posts for clarity, accessibility, and consistency. Suggest concrete improvements without changing the brand voice. Posts: [posts]

:demo-learn-beginner.content: Teach me [topic] from zero. Explain the core idea with an everyday analogy, then give one worked example and a short practice question.

:demo-learn-socratic.content: Help me learn [topic] by asking one question at a time. Wait for my answer, then give feedback and the next question.

:demo-learn-flashcards.content: Create 15 flashcards for [topic]. Put a precise question on the front and a concise answer with a memory cue on the back.

:demo-learn-quiz.content: Quiz me on [topic] with 10 mixed-difficulty questions. Do not reveal answers until I respond; then explain my mistakes.

:demo-learn-plan.content: Build a four-week study plan for [skill] with 30 minutes per day. Include practice, review, milestones, and a final project.

:demo-learn-analogy.content: Explain [concept] using two different analogies. Show where each analogy is useful and where it breaks down.

:demo-learn-compare.content: Compare [concept A] and [concept B] for a beginner. Cover purpose, similarities, differences, an example, and when to use each.

:demo-learn-check.content: Ask me five questions that reveal whether I truly understand [topic], not just memorized definitions. Explain what each tests.

:demo-learn-summary.content: Summarize these notes as key ideas, definitions, and open questions. Highlight anything that seems contradictory. Notes: [notes]

:demo-learn-teachback.content: I will explain [topic] in my own words. Check my explanation for gaps or mistakes, then suggest one focused improvement. My explanation: [text]

:demo-research-question.content: Turn this broad interest into five answerable research questions. For each, suggest what evidence would be needed. Interest: [topic]

:demo-research-plan.content: Design a research plan for [question]. Include scope, search terms, primary-source types, credibility checks, and a way to record uncertainty.

:demo-research-sources.content: Suggest the kinds of primary sources that could answer [question]. Explain what each can and cannot establish. Do not invent citations.

:demo-research-compare.content: Compare these sources on methods, evidence, limitations, and agreement. Quote only from provided text and flag missing context. Sources: [sources]

:demo-research-claims.content: Extract the factual claims from this passage. For each, say what evidence would verify it and label opinion or inference clearly. Passage: [text]

:demo-research-interview.content: Draft an interview guide for exploring [topic]. Begin with open questions, add neutral follow-ups, and avoid leading language.

:demo-research-gaps.content: Review this summary and identify unanswered questions, assumptions, conflicting evidence, and the next most valuable check. Summary: [text]

:demo-research-notes.content: Organize these research notes into findings, supporting evidence, uncertainties, and source details. Do not merge distinct claims. Notes: [notes]

:demo-research-bias.content: Assess potential bias in this research design. Consider selection, measurement, confounding, and interpretation; suggest practical mitigations. Design: [design]

:demo-research-synthesis.content: Synthesize the provided evidence into a short answer to [question]. Distinguish strong findings from tentative inferences and cite the supplied sources. Evidence: [text]

:demo-code-explain.content: Explain this code to a developer new to the project. Cover inputs, outputs, side effects, and one likely edge case. Code: [code]

:demo-code-review.content: Review this code for correctness, security, readability, and test gaps. Prioritize actionable findings with file and line references. Code: [code]

:demo-code-debug.content: Help debug this failure. First summarize observed behavior, then list likely causes ranked by evidence and the smallest test for each. Error and code: [details]

:demo-code-tests.content: Propose tests for [function or feature]. Cover the happy path, boundaries, invalid input, and a regression case; state assumptions.

:demo-code-refactor.content: Suggest a minimal refactor for this code. Preserve behavior and public interfaces, explain trade-offs, and show how to verify parity. Code: [code]

:demo-code-docs.content: Write practical documentation for [API or function] with purpose, parameters, return value, errors, and a small realistic example.

:demo-code-commit.content: Write a concise commit message and body from these changes. Explain what changed and why; do not claim tests that were not run. Changes: [diff]

:demo-code-design.content: Compare two implementation approaches for [feature]. Evaluate complexity, failure modes, performance, and migration cost before recommending one.

:demo-code-performance.content: Analyze this slow path. Identify measurable bottlenecks, propose profiling steps, and suggest optimizations only where the evidence supports them. Code: [code]

:demo-code-security.content: Threat-model [feature]. List assets, trust boundaries, realistic attack paths, and mitigations, separating must-fix issues from defense in depth.

:demo-data-clean.content: Create a data-cleaning plan for [dataset]. Cover missing values, duplicates, inconsistent formats, outliers, and validation without silently discarding records.

:demo-data-summary.content: Summarize this dataset for a nontechnical reader. Explain what each metric means, the biggest patterns, and the limitations. Data: [data]

:demo-data-chart.content: Recommend the clearest chart for [question] using [columns]. Explain the axes, grouping, and one misleading presentation to avoid.

:demo-data-sql.content: Write a readable SQL query for [question] using this schema: [schema]. State assumptions, handle nulls deliberately, and explain the result.

:demo-data-formula.content: Suggest a spreadsheet formula for [task] given these columns: [columns]. Explain the formula and an example row; mention version-specific functions if used.

:demo-data-compare.content: Compare these two periods using absolute and percentage changes. Highlight denominator pitfalls and avoid causal claims. Data: [data]

:demo-data-quality.content: Design data-quality checks for [table]. Include types, ranges, uniqueness, referential integrity, freshness, and example failure messages.

:demo-data-experiment.content: Outline how to analyze this experiment. Define the primary metric, guardrails, segments, and uncertainty before looking at results. Setup: [setup]

:demo-data-story.content: Turn these findings into a clear data story with context, key result, caveats, and an actionable next question. Findings: [data]

:demo-data-dictionary.content: Draft a data dictionary for these fields with definition, type, allowed values, null meaning, and an example. Fields: [fields]

:demo-plan-project.content: Make a project plan for [goal] with milestones, dependencies, owners, risks, and a realistic first step. State what is unknown.

:demo-plan-week.content: Plan my week around these commitments and priorities. Leave buffer time and identify what should be deferred. Inputs: [schedule and priorities]

:demo-plan-event.content: Create an event checklist for [event] covering preparation, day-of roles, accessibility, contingencies, and follow-up.

:demo-plan-travel.content: Draft a flexible itinerary for [destination and dates]. Group nearby activities, include rest, and mark items that require current-price or opening-hour checks.

:demo-plan-goal.content: Turn [goal] into a measurable 90-day plan. Include weekly actions, leading indicators, obstacles, and a monthly review.

:demo-plan-risk.content: Create a risk register for [project]. Rate likelihood and impact, add early warning signs, owners, and practical mitigations.

:demo-plan-decision.content: Build a decision matrix for [options]. Propose weighted criteria, show key trade-offs, and identify what information could change the decision.

:demo-plan-meeting.content: Create a 30-minute meeting agenda for [outcome]. Assign time boxes, pre-read, decision points, and a clear end state.

:demo-plan-backup.content: Develop a fallback plan for [event or project]. List likely disruptions, trigger points, backup actions, and who communicates changes.

:demo-plan-review.content: Run a retrospective on [project]. Ask what worked, what surprised us, what to change, and which two improvements to try next.

:demo-focus-prioritize.content: Help prioritize this task list by impact, urgency, effort, and dependencies. Explain the top three choices and what can wait. Tasks: [tasks]

:demo-focus-timebox.content: Turn [task] into a focused 45-minute work session with a concrete deliverable, milestones, and a stopping rule.

:demo-focus-breakdown.content: Break this overwhelming task into actions that each take 15 minutes or less. Put the easiest meaningful first step at the top. Task: [task]

:demo-focus-inbox.content: Help process these inbox items. Sort into reply, delegate, schedule, archive, or investigate, with a short reason for each. Items: [items]

:demo-focus-routine.content: Design a sustainable daily routine for [goal] around these constraints: [constraints]. Include a small minimum version for difficult days.

:demo-focus-delegate.content: Draft a delegation brief for [task] with desired outcome, context, boundaries, deadline, and check-in points.

:demo-focus-standup.content: Turn these notes into a concise stand-up update: done, next, blockers, and help needed. Notes: [notes]

:demo-focus-review.content: Guide a 10-minute end-of-day review. Ask about progress, unfinished work, tomorrow's top priority, and one improvement.

:demo-focus-automate.content: Find repetitive steps in this workflow. Suggest low-risk automation ideas, expected savings, and checks to prevent mistakes. Workflow: [steps]

:demo-focus-boundary.content: Write a polite message setting a boundary around [request or availability]. Be clear about what I can do and when.

:demo-business-proposal.content: Draft a one-page proposal for [idea]. Include problem, solution, expected value, cost assumptions, risks, and a specific decision request.

:demo-business-pitch.content: Write a 60-second pitch for [product or idea] aimed at [audience]. Make the problem and differentiator concrete; avoid hype.

:demo-business-swot.content: Create a cautious SWOT analysis for [business or idea]. Separate known facts from assumptions and suggest what to validate next.

:demo-business-customer.content: Map the customer journey for [service] from first awareness to support. Include questions, friction, and possible improvements at each stage.

:demo-business-pricing.content: Outline pricing options for [product] using costs, perceived value, competitor positioning, and customer segments. Flag data needed before setting a price.

:demo-business-negotiation.content: Prepare for a negotiation about [issue]. Clarify priorities, walk-away point, likely interests on both sides, and respectful questions to ask.

:demo-business-kpi.content: Suggest a small set of useful KPIs for [goal]. For each, define calculation, data source, review frequency, and how it could be gamed.

:demo-business-process.content: Document this business process as trigger, steps, owner, exceptions, and completion check. Process: [notes]

:demo-business-brief.content: Write an executive brief on [topic] with decision needed, evidence, options, risks, and recommended next step. Mark assumptions clearly.

:demo-business-feedback.content: Turn these customer comments into themes, representative evidence, frequency caveats, and possible product actions. Comments: [comments]

:demo-creative-names.content: Brainstorm 20 names for [project]. Divide them into descriptive, evocative, playful, and minimalist styles. Flag any names that might need trademark checks.

:demo-creative-character.content: Create a nuanced character for [setting] with desire, fear, contradiction, voice, and a choice that reveals personality.

:demo-creative-scene.content: Write a scene in which [characters] disagree about [issue]. Convey tension through dialogue and subtext, not exposition.

:demo-creative-poem.content: Write a short free-verse poem about [image or feeling]. Use concrete sensory details and avoid familiar clichés.

:demo-creative-world.content: Invent a believable setting for [genre]. Describe daily life, one unusual rule, who benefits from it, and an emerging conflict.

:demo-creative-ideas.content: Generate 15 unusual but feasible ideas for [challenge]. Combine at least three different perspectives and explain the strongest three.

:demo-creative-dialogue.content: Write natural dialogue between [people] about [topic]. Give each a distinct voice and make the exchange reveal something new.

:demo-creative-prompt.content: Create 10 writing prompts around [theme], ranging from realistic to speculative. Each should contain a character, tension, and a constraint.

:demo-creative-twist.content: Offer five surprising but earned twists for this story setup. Explain what earlier clue would make each fair. Setup: [story]

:demo-creative-mood.content: Rewrite this paragraph in three moods: hopeful, ominous, and comic. Preserve the event but change imagery and rhythm. Paragraph: [text]

:demo-translate-faithful.content: Translate the following text into [target language]. Preserve meaning, register, names, and formatting. Flag any phrase with no direct equivalent. Text: [text]

:demo-translate-natural.content: Translate this text into natural [target language] for [audience]. Prioritize idiomatic phrasing while keeping all factual details. Text: [text]

:demo-translate-bosnian.content: Translate the following into standard Bosnian using Latin script. Keep the original tone and do not add information. Text: [text]

:demo-translate-english.content: Translate this text into clear English. Preserve the speaker's intent and note any ambiguous words. Text: [text]

:demo-translate-formal.content: Translate this message into formal [target language] suitable for a professional email. Keep dates, names, and requests exact. Message: [text]

:demo-translate-casual.content: Translate this message into casual but respectful [target language]. Avoid slang that is too regional. Message: [text]

:demo-translate-compare.content: Give two translations of this sentence into [target language]: literal and natural. Explain the important difference. Sentence: [text]

:demo-translate-proof.content: Compare the original and translation for omissions, added meaning, terminology, and tone. Suggest corrections only where needed. Original: [text] Translation: [text]

:demo-translate-glossary.content: Create a bilingual terminology glossary for this text in [source language] and [target language]. Include context notes for ambiguous terms. Text: [text]

:demo-translate-localize.content: Localize this UI text for [locale]. Keep labels short, preserve placeholders exactly, and flag strings that need more context. Strings: [text]

:demo-personal-journal.content: Give me five gentle journaling questions about [experience]. Focus on observations, feelings, needs, and one small next step without judging me.

:demo-personal-reflect.content: Help me reflect on this week. Ask what energized me, what drained me, what I learned, and one thing to change next week.

:demo-personal-habit.content: Design a tiny habit for [goal] that takes under two minutes. Include a trigger, a simple tracker, and a recovery plan for missed days.

:demo-personal-choice.content: Help me think through [decision] without deciding for me. Clarify my values, options, trade-offs, and what information I still need.

:demo-personal-gratitude.content: Help me write a specific note of appreciation to [person]. Mention what they did and why it mattered, without sounding generic.

:demo-personal-celebrate.content: Help me acknowledge a small win: [win]. Reflect on what made it possible and how to carry that forward, without exaggeration.

:demo-personal-conversation.content: Prepare a respectful conversation about [issue]. Help me state observations, feelings, needs, and a clear request while leaving room to listen.

:demo-personal-checkin.content: Guide a quick personal check-in. Ask about my energy, stress, priorities, and what support or rest I may need today.

:demo-personal-weekend.content: Suggest a balanced weekend plan based on [interests and constraints]. Include rest, one useful task, and one enjoyable activity.

:demo-personal-letter.content: Help me draft a letter to my future self about [goal or transition]. Make it honest, encouraging, and grounded in concrete actions.
